data.title: Single Page
data.tagline: Arrange a complete story in sections down one scrolling page
data.description: A single-page layout guides visitors through a sequence such as value, proof, features, pricing, and action. It works when the story has one main goal. Clear sections and anchor navigation help, but important content should not depend on scroll effects.

use: A focused site with one main conversion goal
avoid: Force a large multi-purpose product into one endless page
Hide content behind complex scroll animation
Repeat the same action after every short paragraph
Use sections with no clear narrative order

lessonPractice.title: A product landing page serves one trial goal through a sequence of problem, value, product evidence, customer proof, and action. How should it be organized?

options.label: Use a single scrolling page with ordered sections, anchors, and contextual action entries
options.feedback: All content supports one decision, so a continuous page keeps one reading order while in-page navigation keeps people oriented on a long page.

options.label: Append account, billing, and project management below the landing page and handle everything by scrolling
options.feedback: Those are separate tool tasks rather than one reading path, so merging them confuses navigation and state.

options.label: Give every short section a separate URL and require page-by-page navigation to read everything
options.feedback: The content forms one continuous decision, and excessive page breaks interrupt context and reading rhythm.

data.agentPrompt: Organize the landing page as one scrolling sequence: problem, value, product evidence, customer proof, and CTA. Give sections stable anchors and long-page return paths, and repeat the same primary action only at useful decision stages.

references.title: The Fold Manifesto: Why the Page Fold Still Matters
